Reliability in measurement refers to the consistency and stability of a measure over time or across different conditions. It is about whether the measure produces similar results under consistent circumstances.  

Option (A) is more about whether the measure has any validity or meaning at all, which is not the definition of reliability.  
Option (B) describes validity, not reliability.  
Option (C) correctly captures the idea of consistency in measurement.  
Option (D) is irrelevant to the concept of reliability.  

Final answer: (C)
